title: Hunger Games leads Thanksgiving box office as Hexed and Focker open
body_md:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping maintained its lead at the North American box office on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, collecting $15 million ahead of Thanksgiving. The Lionsgate prequel, which opened the previous weekend, outperformed two new releases and entered the holiday period with continued momentum.

According to the report published on November 26, the film is projected to earn approximately $85 million over the five-day holiday frame. If that forecast holds, its cumulative domestic gross will reach $233 million. Positive audience recommendations are cited as a factor supporting its performance beyond the opening weekend.

Disney's animated fantasy Hexed earned $7.6 million on its opening day from 3,725 theaters. Universal's comedy Focker In-Law followed with $5.3 million from 3,382 locations. The comedy did not hold Tuesday preview screenings, meaning its Wednesday figure reflects the first day of public showtimes.

Despite Disney's initial advantage, updated forecasts suggest Focker In-Law could finish the holiday in second place. Hexed is projected to collect between $31 million and $35 million over five days, while the comedy is targeting $35 million to $36 million. Both estimates are below earlier expectations of $40 million to $45 million.

The financial stakes are particularly significant for Hexed, whose reported production budget exceeds $200 million. International ticket sales and sustained attendance throughout the holiday season will be important because theatrical revenue is shared with exhibitors. An A- CinemaScore offers an encouraging indication of audience reception, although it cannot guarantee strong long-term earnings.

Focker In-Law, co-financed by Universal and Paramount for a reported $90 million, revisits the family comedy franchise featuring Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro. Ariana Grande joins the cast as the girlfriend of Greg's son Henry, played by Skyler Gisondo. The film received a 29 percent Rotten Tomatoes critics score in the report, while audiences awarded it a B+ CinemaScore.

The wider holiday marketplace is expected to generate between $210 million and $215 million across all releases. That would fall well below the record $422 million Thanksgiving period of 2024. Nevertheless, the report indicates that domestic ticket sales for the year are running approximately 20 percent ahead of the corresponding point in 2025.

The Wednesday results establish an early advantage for Sunrise on the Reaping, but the relative positions of the two newcomers could change as families and other audiences visit theaters throughout the holiday. Five-day grosses remain projections rather than confirmed final totals.
excerpt: Sunrise on the Reaping leads Wednesday with $15 million as two new releases compete.
